name: Thunder & Lightning

name: Turner & Hooch

tenures.note: Michael Turner: 6'6", 276 lbs, Atlanta, GA, face — a former University of Georgia running back who trained at a Steel Cage Wrestling school alongside childhood friend Isaac "Hooch" Johnson before UPW signed them as a team. Turned down the Warriors' own recruitment pitch (4 October 2016) and lost the Down South Connection's own in-ring debut (17 January 2017); Johnson also wrestled once without his partner, losing to Derek Rage (29 December 2016).

tenures.source: The federation's own tag-team application page (openertagapp04.html) and its own card for 11 February 2020 (schedule.html), which bills the team's SCW debut.
tenures.note: Billed only: no held SCW broadcast stages the team. The 11 February 2020 card reads "In a tag team debut, Michael Turner and Isaac \"Hooch\" Johnson make their entrance into SCW's tag team division with a battle against Thunder & Lightening!"

caption: Michael Turner and Isaac "Hooch" Johnson wrestled UPW as Turner & Hooch, a tag team built on a friendship that began on a Georgia high school football field.

identity.note: One team across UPW and SCW. UPW gladly obligated and accepted the two as a tag team"). SCW's own card for 11 February 2020 books them against Thunder & Lightning in "a tag team debut" for "the journeyman duo", the same match UPW's own card for 25 April 2017 had booked and never played.

name: The Warriors

tenures.role: tag team — UPW World Tag Team Champions (one reign)
tenures.note: Managed by Sammy Sharifi. Won UPW's own first World Tag Team Championship from the Hype on the debut Showdown (9/20/2016), casting the win as a stand against racism in wrestling. Lost the belts to Soldiers of the Sun at Survival on 5 March 2017. Retained the belts by disqualification when a still-defected Titan Juarez ran in against the Dominion (17 January 2017), and again in a non-title match when the Dominion's own interference against Juarez drew a DQ the other way (18 February 2017).

caption: DeAwn Carter and Kel Robertson, the Warriors, became UPW's own first World Tag Team Champions on the promotion's debut show and cast their reign as a stand against the business's own bigotry, holding the belts until Survival.

identity.note: "The Warriors" is a common enough tag-team label that CSWA alone fields two other teams sharing the word (Boulevard Warriors, Indian Warriors) and a third registered team (the-dream-warriors) shares it too — none in the same fed or era as UPW's own Warriors (DeAwn Carter and Kel Robertson), and nothing in either record connects them; recorded distinct per the no-auto-merge rule.

name: The Hype

tenures.note: Challenged the Warriors for UPW's own first World Tag Team Championship on the promotion's debut show (9/20/2016) and lost, two falls to one. Beat the Brothers Grimm on 4 October 2016. A scheduled 13 December 2016 match against the O'Malley Brothers was scrapped when the Dominion ambushed the Hype with chairs beforehand.

caption: The Hype, Danny Nash and Messer, challenged for UPW's own first World Tag Team Championship on the promotion's debut show and came up short.

name: Soldiers of the Sun

tenures.role: tag team/trio — UPW World Tag Team Champions (one reign)
tenures.note: Introduced on UPW's own broadcast as the number-one contenders for the World Tag Team Championship. Won the belts from the Warriors at Survival on 5 March 2017, in a Fatal Four-Way also involving the Dominion and the O'Malley Brothers, and held them through UPW's own final months. Won their own in-ring UPW debut over the Brothers Grimm (20 September 2016) and beat Turner & Hooch (4 October 2016). Weathered Titan Juarez's own mid-season defection to the Warriors (29 December 2016 through 17 January 2017) before he rejoined for good, and retained the tag titles against the Down South Connection on UPW's own final broadcast (11 April 2017).

caption: Soldiers of the Sun — Ricky Courage, STRIKER Kato and Titan Juarez — won UPW's own World Tag Team Championship at Survival in a fatal four-way and held the belts through the promotion's own final months.

name: The Dominion

tenures.note: Interfered at ringside throughout Windham Brody's Television Title win over Brandon Franklin on 11 April 2017, working over Franklin's shoulder on De Luca's own instruction. Formed on UPW's own second broadcast (4 October 2016) when Donovan and Bishop ran in to help De Luca beat Liam Donegal; won their own in-ring debut over the Hype the same night as it aired (8 November 2016). Ran a season-long program against the O'Malley Brothers, ambushed the Hype and a six-man tag involving Caleb Foley, and interfered in De Luca's own North American Championship tournament win (18 February 2017) before helping Windham Brody take the Television Championship (11 April 2017) and ambushing Ricky Courage on the entrance ramp the same night.

caption: The Dominion — Antonio De Luca, Tyson Bishop and Lance Donovan — ran together as a stable through UPW's own final year, De Luca's own North American Championship reign chief among their spoils.

identity.note: XCWF's own minion-xcwf shares no name beyond a coincidental normalized-substring match ("The Dominion" containing "Minion") with this UPW stable — different fed, different era, no evidence connecting the two; recorded distinct per the no-auto-merge rule.

name: The O'Malley Brothers

tenures.note: An Irish/Italian-gimmicked tag team whose UPW debut against the Hype was scrapped three separate times by Dominion interference. Earned a World Tag Team Championship shot at Survival (5 March 2017) in the same Fatal Four-Way that crowned Soldiers of the Sun, alongside the Warriors and the Dominion, but did not win the belts.

caption: The O'Malley Brothers spent UPW's own back half feuding with the Dominion, their in-ring debut scrapped three times before a Survival title shot came up empty.

name: Down South Connection

tenures.note: Debuted with a promo trashing UPW's own tag division (29 December 2016), then won their in-ring debut over Michael Turner and Isaac "Hooch" Johnson with a chair-assisted finish (17 January 2017). Lost to champions Soldiers of the Sun on UPW's own final broadcast (11 April 2017).

caption: The Down South Connection talked up UPW's own tag division before backing it up in their debut win, though a title shot against Soldiers of the Sun came up short on the promotion's final show.

identity.note: The registry's own aka-collision guard reads "Connection" as a normalized substring match against a registered entity literally named "Connection"; different fed, nothing connecting the two beyond the shared word. Recorded distinct per the no-auto-merge rule.

name: Columbus Crushers

tenures.note: Lost the one match the surviving record holds for them, a special-referee tag against Soldiers of the Sun worked by a comically biased Sammy Sharifi (13 December 2016), despite the referee's own favoritism.

caption: The Columbus Crushers lost the one UPW match the surviving record holds for them, despite a referee stacked in their favor.
